# ONNX model authoring

For durable account-backed work, use authenticated MCP and preserve the exact
ONNX artifact and checksum through an opaque fetched resource ID or another
server-supported artifact reference. Do not embed model bytes in generated JSON.
For deliberately local or offline work, keep the artifact and checksum in the
local project and use the local Biosimulant CLI (`biosimulant`); do not claim a Gateway revision,
run, or Passport. Record model origin, training-data claims that are actually
supported, ONNX opset, runtime version, hardware needs, preprocessing,
postprocessing, class labels, and tensor names/dtypes/shapes.

Expose deliberate typed ports rather than raw ambiguous tensors. Test graph loading, input validation, deterministic fixtures where applicable, output shape and label mapping, unsupported operators, and CPU/GPU behavior. Distinguish technical graph execution from biological validation. Include calibration, uncertainty, domain-shift, and non-use caveats; never infer therapeutic or clinical meaning from a model score alone.

When opting into model compatibility, declare tensor layout, axes, ordered
feature labels, identifier namespace/version, preprocessing normalization,
endpoint meaning, cohort/context, origin, and uncertainty under the existing
ports' contracts. A matching tensor shape alone is not biological compatibility.

A finite ONNX wrapper uses `execute(inputs, *, context)` with the imported enum
member `ExecutionPolicy.ONCE_BEFORE_RUN`. Do not use the quoted uppercase string
`"ONCE_BEFORE_RUN"`; its literal runtime value is `"once_before_run"`.


## Visualization deliverables

Before authoring, call `get_biosimulant_authoring_contract` with topic `visualization`.
The complete catalog contains timeseries, bar, scatter, heatmap, graph, table, image,
structure3d and text, including payload examples, limits and retained artifact rules.
Almost every scientific Lab needs a useful visual of actual computed outputs; choose
the type by the user's question rather than always emitting a table. Record expected
views, source outputs, units and caveats in the MRS; record render/schema, owning module,
typed wiring, lifecycle, artifact retention and executable checks in the MTS.
Implement reusable `BioModule.visualize()` and declare `lab.yaml` visualization requirements
(or a justified opt-out for infrastructure-only work). Inspect actual composed results,
check plotted values against typed outputs, and verify artifacts and reopening. Missing
or invalid required views block qualification/publication. Ad-hoc Studio chat charts
do not satisfy this contract. Historical Labs without a declaration remain compatible.
